explanation.text:
Here begins the second part of the book, Pro. 10:1-22:16, which, with the third, Pro. 22:16-25:28, contains series of proverbs whose sense is complete in one or two verses, and which, having no logical connection, admit of no analysis. The parallelisms of Pro. 10:1-15:33 are mostly antithetic; and those of Pro. 16:1-22:16, synthetic. The evidences of art in the structure are very clear, and indicate, probably, a purpose of facilitating the labor of memorizing. (Pro. 10:1-32)

wise [and] foolish--as they follow or reject the precepts of wisdom.

maketh . . . father--or, "gladdens a father."

heaviness--or, "grief."

bsb.text: The proverbs of Solomon: A wise son brings joy to his father, but a foolish son grief to his mother.

explanation.text:
Treasures . . . nothing--that is, Ill-gotten gains give no true happiness (compare Pro 4:17; Mat 6:19).

righteousness--especially beneficence (Psa 112:9).

death--the greatest of all evils.

bsb.text: Ill-gotten treasures profit nothing, but righteousness brings deliverance from death.

explanation.text: (Compare Psa 37:16-20). The last clause is better: "He will repel the greedy desires of the wicked."

bsb.text: The LORD does not let the righteous go hungry, but He denies the craving of the wicked.

explanation.text:
slack--literally, "deceitful," failing of its purpose (compare Hos 7:16).

maketh rich--(compare Pro 10:22).

bsb.text: Idle hands make one poor, but diligent hands bring wealth.

explanation.text:
son--as Pro 1:8, Pro 1:10, and often.

sleepeth--in indolence, and not for rest.

causeth shame--literally, "is base" (compare Pro 14:35; Pro 17:2).

bsb.text: He who gathers in summer is a wise son, but he who sleeps during harvest is a disgraceful son.

explanation.text: Blessings--literally, "Praises." The last clause is better: "The mouth of the wicked covereth (or concealeth) violence (or mischievous devices)" to be executed in due time (Psa 5:9; Psa 10:7; Rom 3:14), and hence has no praises (compare Pro 10:11).

bsb.text: Blessings are on the head of the righteous, but the mouth of the wicked conceals violence.

explanation.text:
blessed--literally, "for a blessing," or praise.

shall rot--literally, "be worm-eaten," useless and disgusting.

bsb.text: The memory of the righteous is a blessing, but the name of the wicked will rot.

explanation.text:
wise, etc.--(compare Pro 9:8-9, Pro 9:16), opposed to

prating fool--or, "fool of lips of wicked language."

fall--headlong, suddenly.

bsb.text: A wise heart will receive commandments, but foolish lips will come to ruin.

explanation.text:
perverteth his ways--acts deceitfully.

known--discovered and punished.

bsb.text: He who walks in integrity walks securely, but he who perverts his ways will be found out.

explanation.text: Two vices contrasted; hypocrisy, or insinuating evil against one (Pro 6:13; Psa 35:19), and rashness of speech. In each case, the results are on the evildoers.

bsb.text: He who winks the eye causes grief, and foolish lips will come to ruin.

explanation.text: a well--or, "source" of good to himself and others (Joh 7:37-38). On last clause, see on Pro 10:6.

bsb.text: The mouth of the righteous is a fountain of life, but the mouth of the wicked conceals violence.

explanation.text:
strifes--or, "litigations."

covereth--by forgiveness and forbearance.

bsb.text: Hatred stirs up dissension, but love covers all transgressions.

explanation.text:
In the lips . . . found--hence, not beaten, as the wicked-speaking fool.

void of understanding-- (Pro 6:32; Pro 7:7).

bsb.text: Wisdom is found on the lips of the discerning, but a rod is for the back of him who lacks judgment.

explanation.text:
lay up knowledge--that is, as treasures for good use.

mouth . . . destruction--or, "as to the mouth," etc., destruction is near; they expose themselves to evil by prating.

bsb.text: The wise store up knowledge, but the mouth of the fool invites destruction.

explanation.text: Both by trusting in "uncertain riches" (Ti1 6:17), or by the evils of poverty (Pro 30:9), men, not fearing God, fall into dangers.

bsb.text: The wealth of the rich man is his fortified city, but poverty is the ruin of the poor.

explanation.text: The industry of the righteous is alone truly successful, while the earnings of the wicked tempt and lead to sin.

bsb.text: The labor of the righteous leads to life, but the gain of the wicked brings punishment.

explanation.text:
keepeth--observes (Pro 3:18; Pro 4:22).

refuseth--or, "turns from reproof," which might direct him aright.

bsb.text: Whoever heeds instruction is on the path to life, but he who ignores reproof goes astray.

explanation.text: Both vices must one day be known and punished, and hence their folly.

bsb.text: The one who conceals hatred has lying lips, and whoever spreads slander is a fool.

explanation.text: Much speech involves risk of sin; hence the wisdom of restraining the tongue (Psa 39:1; Jam 1:26).

bsb.text: When words are many, sin is unavoidable, but he who restrains his lips is wise.

explanation.text: Right speech is the fruit of a good heart, but the wicked show theirs to be useless.

bsb.text: The tongue of the righteous is choice silver, but the heart of the wicked has little worth.

explanation.text: Fools not only fail to benefit others, as do the righteous, but procure their own ruin (compare Pro 10:11, Pro 10:17; Hos 4:6).

bsb.text: The lips of the righteous feed many, but fools die for lack of judgment.

explanation.text: it maketh, etc.--"it" is emphatic. Riches from God are without the sorrow of ill-gotten wealth (compare Ecc 2:21-23; Ti1 6:9-10, Ti1 6:17).

bsb.text: The blessing of the LORD enriches, and He adds no sorrow to it.

explanation.text: Sin is the pleasure of the wicked; wisdom that of the good.

bsb.text: The fool delights in shameful conduct, but a man of understanding has wisdom.

explanation.text: it--the very thing. The wicked get dreaded evil; the righteous, desired good.

bsb.text: What the wicked man dreads will overtake him, but the desire of the righteous will be granted.

explanation.text:
(Compare Psa 1:4; Psa 37:9-10, Psa 37:36).

righteous . . . foundation--well laid and firm (Mat 7:24-25).

bsb.text: When the whirlwind passes, the wicked are no more, but the righteous are secure forever.

explanation.text: that is, causes vexation.

bsb.text: Like vinegar to the teeth and smoke to the eyes, so is the slacker to those who send him.

explanation.text: (Compare Pro 9:11; Psa 55:23).

bsb.text: The fear of the LORD prolongs life, but the years of the wicked will be cut short.

explanation.text:
gladness--in confidence of realizing it.

expectation . . . perish--in disappointment.

bsb.text: The hope of the righteous is joy, but the expectations of the wicked will perish.

explanation.text: The way, etc.--that is, God's providence sustains the righteous and overthrows the wicked (Hos 14:9).

bsb.text: The way of the LORD is a refuge to the upright, but destruction awaits those who do evil.

explanation.text:
(Compare Pro 12:3; Psa 37:9-11; Psa 102:28).

earth--or, "land of promise."

bsb.text: The righteous will never be shaken, but the wicked will not inhabit the land.

explanation.text:
bringeth forth--literally, "germinates" as a plant.

froward--(Compare Pro 2:12, Pro 2:14).

cut off--as an unproductive plant.

bsb.text: The mouth of the righteous brings forth wisdom, but a perverse tongue will be cut out.

explanation.text:
know--regard and provide for (Psa 1:6).

frowardness--all kinds of deceit and ill-nature. The word is plural.

bsb.text: The lips of the righteous know what is fitting, but the mouth of the wicked is perverse.
